product.name: Private Media Vault
product.purpose: Provide an on-device iOS and iPadOS private media library that protects against casual snooping and deliberate entry attempts on an unlocked device, preserves original media fidelity, supports useful organization/search/viewing/acquisition workflows, and keeps vault-derived data local except for explicit user-directed outbound or explicitly enabled backup capabilities.

primary_users.role: Privacy-conscious iPhone or iPad owner managing personal media
primary_users.technical_level: General consumer; must not need security or file-management expertise
primary_users.work_context: Uses the app as a real private photo/video library, discreet utility surface, local browser/acquisition tool, and explicit export/recovery boundary on a personal Apple device.

jobs_to_be_done.statement: Open the app into a genuinely useful calculator decoy that does not reveal or depend on vault state.
Enter and leave the private vault discreetly while preserving a real credential boundary and predictable lock behavior.
Import, preserve, browse, view, organize, favorite, and delete private photos and videos without losing original fidelity or creating hidden duplicate semantics.
Bring media in from Files, Photos, sharing, browser downloads, and drag-and-drop through one durable recoverable ingestion model.
Use albums, folders, metadata search, filters, and local-only search intelligence to find private media without exposing it to external services.
View stills, videos, Live Photos, RAW, animated media, and slideshows with native-feeling controls and predictable lifecycle/privacy behavior.
Use an isolated in-app browser for normal web navigation and explicitly save supported media into the vault without scraping or restriction circumvention.
Explicitly share, save, export originals, permanently delete media, reset an inaccessible vault, and restore supported canonical state without ambiguous data-loss semantics.
Understand and control locking, storage, diagnostics, generated data, browser data, backup participation, accessibility, and system exposure without hidden telemetry or network leakage.
Purchase or restore the permanent Pro entitlement for expanded capabilities without subscriptions, launch paywalls, data loss, or loss of access when entitlement later changes.

must_reduce: Risk that private media or vault-derived metadata is exposed outside the authenticated app without explicit user action
Risk of losing accepted media during import, interruption, low storage, migration, entitlement change, or process lifecycle events
Friction in using the product as a real photo and video library rather than merely a hidden folder
Need for users to understand internal storage, security, persistence, or media-resource implementation details
Behavioral inconsistency between acquisition, viewing, organization, export, and lifecycle paths
must_not_become: A cloud account or backend service for vault-derived data
A fake calculator whose only purpose is to hide an unlock gesture
A subscription product or paywall that traps existing user data
A hidden general-purpose file manager or DRM/restriction circumvention tool
A product that claims forensic secure deletion or replaces platform security with custom cryptography
An analytics, advertising, remote-crash, developer-telemetry, or cloud-ML collection surface
A codebase whose domain vocabulary or architecture is coupled to the consumer marketing brand
experience_principles: Authentication is the real security boundary; camouflage and decoy behavior are secondary and must remain credible
Preserve canonical originals and make generated derivatives disposable and rebuildable
Prefer Apple-native platform behavior and UI where it satisfies the product contract
Keep vault-derived data on device except for explicit user-directed outbound actions or explicitly enabled backup behavior
Never silently lose accepted work; interruption and partial failure should remain inspectable and recoverable
Free-tier or entitlement changes must never hide, delete, or block access to existing user media
Keep calculator, vault, browser, generated search data, and other persistence domains isolated according to their lifecycle contracts
Use deterministic tests and snapshots at public behavior/transformation seams rather than coupling tests to private implementation details
Accessibility, iPad adaptability, and system preferences are release requirements rather than optional polish
Keep consumer identity at release/configuration boundaries and use brand-neutral domain terminology
